key_insight: There is no single best model for producing diverse valid answers; training a learned "router" to pick among models/sampling strategies per prompt yields far better coverage of unique high-quality responses.
problem_solved: How to comprehensively generate the full range of valid answers for prompts that admit many correct responses, avoiding redundancy and missed valid options from single-model sampling.
method: Introduce a metric called diversity coverage that scores the total quality of unique answers in a predicted set relative to the optimal set of the same size.
Train a lightweight router that, given a prompt, selects among candidate models or sampling strategies to maximize diversity coverage rather than per-sample likelihood.
Combine outputs across routed models, deduplicate by answer identity, and optimize routing using feedback derived from answer quality scores.
impact: Practitioners can obtain more comprehensive and non-redundant collections of valid outputs for open-ended tasks (e.g., creative generation, multi-answer QA, data augmentation) by using model routing instead of relying on a single generator or sampling heuristic.
visual_elements: Schematic: prompt → learned router → multiple models/samplers → merged, deduplicated answer set
Bar chart: diversity coverage comparison (single-model vs. router) across answer-set sizes
Annotated example: side-by-side answer lists showing redundancy from one model vs. diverse unique answers from routed ensemble with quality scores
Flow diagram of metric: how diversity coverage is computed (unique answers, quality scoring, normalization vs. optimal set)
paper_title: No Single Best Model for Diversity: Learning a Router for Sample Diversity
paper_authors: Yuhan Liu, Fangyuan Xu, Vishakh Padmakumar, Daphne Ippolito, Eunsol Choi
